q: The Harappan site of Lothal, known for its dockyard, is located in which present-day state?
x: Lothal, in Gujarat, has a large brick basin generally identified as a dockyard, pointing to sea trade with West Asia.
e: Gujarat's Harappan sites: Lothal (dockyard), Dholavira (water tanks), Surkotada (horse bones).

q: The Great Bath, a large watertight tank, was found at which Harappan site?
x: The Great Bath at Mohenjodaro is a brick tank made watertight with gypsum mortar and a layer of bitumen, with steps at each end. It is usually read as a site of ritual bathing.
e: Mohenjodaro = Great Bath and the Great Granary; it lies on the Indus in Sindh, Pakistan.

q: Who deciphered the Brahmi script used in Ashoka's edicts?
x: James Prinsep deciphered Brahmi and Kharosthi in 1837, which made it possible to read Ashoka's inscriptions and identify the king called 'Devanampiya Piyadasi' as Ashoka.
e: Prinsep read the script; Cunningham founded the Archaeological Survey of India.

q: Gautama Buddha delivered his first sermon at which place?
x: The Buddha gave his first sermon, the Dhammachakkappavattana Sutta, at the deer park in Sarnath near Varanasi. This event is called the turning of the wheel of law.
e: Lumbini born, Bodh Gaya enlightened, Sarnath first sermon, Kushinagar died.

q: The third Buddhist Council was held during the reign of which ruler?
x: The third Buddhist Council met at Pataliputra under Ashoka, with Moggaliputta Tissa presiding. The fourth was held in Kashmir under Kanishka.
e: Councils: 1st Rajagriha (Ajatashatru), 2nd Vaishali, 3rd Pataliputra (Ashoka), 4th Kashmir (Kanishka).

q: Mahavira, the 24th Tirthankara of Jainism, attained nirvana at which place?
x: Mahavira died and attained nirvana at Pavapuri in present-day Bihar, around 468 BCE by the traditional reckoning.
e: Mahavira: born at Kundagrama near Vaishali, died at Pavapuri.

q: The Allahabad Pillar inscription, which records the conquests of Samudragupta, was composed by whom?
x: Harisena, Samudragupta's court poet, composed the Prayag Prashasti engraved on an older Ashokan pillar at Allahabad.
e: Harisena praised Samudragupta, who is often called the 'Napoleon of India'.

q: The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of which ruler?
x: Fa-Hien travelled in India between about 399 and 414 CE, during the reign of Chandragupta II Vikramaditya. Hiuen Tsang came later, under Harshavardhana.
e: Fa-Hien with the Guptas; Hiuen Tsang with Harsha; Itsing later still.

q: Who was the first woman ruler of the Delhi Sultanate?
x: Razia Sultan, daughter of Iltutmish, ruled Delhi from 1236 to 1240 — the only woman to sit on the throne of the Delhi Sultanate.
e: Iltutmish chose his daughter over his sons; the nobles later removed her.

q: Which Sultan of Delhi shifted the capital from Delhi to Daulatabad?
x: Muhammad bin Tughlaq moved the capital to Devagiri, renamed Daulatabad, around 1327 and ordered the people of Delhi to move there. The experiment failed and the court returned.
e: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's two famous failures: the Daulatabad move and token currency.

q: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded in 1336 by which pair of brothers?
x: Harihara I and Bukka Raya I founded Vijayanagara on the Tungabhadra in 1336, starting the Sangama dynasty. Its ruins are at Hampi in Karnataka.
e: Vijayanagara = 'city of victory'; founded 1336, broken after Talikota in 1565.

q: In which battle was the Vijayanagara Empire decisively defeated in 1565?
x: The combined Deccan Sultanates defeated Vijayanagara at Talikota in 1565; the city of Hampi was sacked afterwards.
e: Talikota 1565 — after it, Hampi was left in the ruins visitors see today.

q: Who founded the Mughal Empire in India after the First Battle of Panipat?
x: Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 and founded the Mughal Empire. He used field artillery and the tulughma formation.
e: Panipat 1526 (Babur), 1556 (Akbar v Hemu), 1761 (Abdali v Marathas).

q: Akbar abolished the jizya tax in which year?
x: Akbar abolished the jizya, the tax on non-Muslims, in 1564, after ending the pilgrimage tax the previous year. Aurangzeb reimposed it in 1679.
e: Akbar removed jizya in 1564; Aurangzeb brought it back in 1679.

q: The Battle of Haldighati in 1576 was fought between Maharana Pratap and the forces of which ruler?
x: At Haldighati in 1576, Maharana Pratap of Mewar fought Akbar's army led by Raja Man Singh of Amber. Pratap withdrew but was never captured.
e: Haldighati 1576: Maharana Pratap and his horse Chetak against Man Singh.

q: Shivaji was formally crowned Chhatrapati in 1674 at which fort?
x: Shivaji's coronation took place at Raigad fort in June 1674, where he took the title Chhatrapati. He was born at Shivneri fort.
e: Born at Shivneri, crowned at Raigad.

q: Who founded the Sikh religion?
x: Guru Nanak (1469-1539) founded Sikhism and was the first of the ten Gurus. Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth, founded the Khalsa in 1699.
e: Ten Gurus: first Nanak, tenth Gobind Singh, then the Guru Granth Sahib itself.

q: The Battle of Buxar in 1764 was fought between the English East India Company and the combined forces of which three leaders?
o: Siraj-ud-daulah, Mir Jafar and Shah Alam II
Tipu Sultan, the Nizam and the Marathas
Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-daulah and Shah Alam II
Mir Jafar, the Nizam and Haider Ali
x: At Buxar in 1764 the Company defeated the joint army of Mir Qasim of Bengal, Shuja-ud-daulah of Awadh and the Mughal emperor Shah Alam II. The Treaty of Allahabad in 1765 then gave the Company the Diwani of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha.
e: Plassey won Bengal by intrigue; Buxar won it in open battle and brought the Diwani.

q: The Permanent Settlement of Bengal in 1793 was introduced by whom?
x: Lord Cornwallis introduced the Permanent Settlement in 1793, fixing the land revenue of Bengal, Bihar and Odisha for ever and making zamindars the owners of the land.
e: Permanent Settlement = Cornwallis + zamindars; Ryotwari = Thomas Munro; Mahalwari = village bodies.

q: The practice of sati was legally abolished in 1829 during the time of which Governor-General?
x: Lord William Bentinck banned sati by Regulation XVII of 1829, supported by Raja Ram Mohan Roy's long campaign against it.
e: Bentinck 1829: sati banned, with Raja Ram Mohan Roy behind the reform.

q: Who is regarded as the father of the Indian Renaissance and founded the Brahmo Samaj?
x: Raja Ram Mohan Roy founded the Brahmo Sabha in 1828, which became the Brahmo Samaj. He campaigned against sati and for women's education.
e: Brahmo Samaj: Ram Mohan Roy, 1828. Arya Samaj: Dayanand Saraswati, 1875.

q: The Arya Samaj was founded in 1875 by whom?
x: Swami Dayanand Saraswati founded the Arya Samaj at Bombay in 1875, with the slogan 'Back to the Vedas'. He wrote Satyarth Prakash.
e: 'Back to the Vedas' — Dayanand Saraswati, Arya Samaj, 1875.

q: The Revolt of 1857 began with the uprising of sepoys at which place?
x: The general revolt broke out at Meerut on 10 May 1857, after which the sepoys marched to Delhi. Mangal Pandey's earlier solo act was at Barrackpore in March 1857.
e: Barrackpore was the spark (Mangal Pandey); Meerut was the fire (10 May 1857).

q: Who was proclaimed the symbolic leader of the Revolt of 1857 at Delhi?
x: The rebel sepoys proclaimed the last Mughal emperor, Bahadur Shah Zafar, as their leader at Delhi. He was later exiled to Rangoon, where he died in 1862.
e: Centres of 1857: Delhi (Bahadur Shah Zafar), Kanpur (Nana Saheb), Jhansi (Rani Lakshmibai), Lucknow (Begum Hazrat Mahal).

q: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by whom?
x: A. O. Hume, a retired British civil servant, founded the Indian National Congress in 1885. Its first session was held in Bombay, with W. C. Bonnerjee as president.
e: Hume founded it; Bonnerjee presided over the first session at Bombay.

q: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 was carried out by which Viceroy?
x: Lord Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905, which set off the Swadeshi movement. The partition was annulled in 1911.
e: Curzon split Bengal in 1905; the protest that followed was the Swadeshi movement.

q: At which session did the Indian National Congress adopt 'Purna Swaraj' as its goal?
x: At the Lahore session of December 1929, presided over by Jawaharlal Nehru, the Congress adopted complete independence as its goal. Independence Day was first observed on 26 January 1930.
e: Lahore 1929 → Purna Swaraj → 26 January, the date later chosen for the Constitution.

q: Which committee was appointed by the British government to inquire into the Jallianwala Bagh massacre?
x: The Hunter Committee, headed by Lord William Hunter, was appointed in 1919 to inquire into the firing at Jallianwala Bagh. The Congress set up its own committee because it found the official inquiry inadequate.
e: The Rowlatt Act led to the protest, Dyer ordered the firing, the Hunter Committee inquired into it.

q: The Non-Cooperation Movement was called off by Gandhi after which incident?
x: After a crowd set fire to a police station at Chauri Chaura in February 1922, killing policemen, Gandhi called off the Non-Cooperation Movement because it had turned violent.
e: Chauri Chaura, February 1922 — the movement stopped because it stopped being non-violent.

q: The Dandi March, which began the Civil Disobedience Movement, started on which date?
x: Gandhi began the Dandi March from Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March 1930 and broke the salt law at Dandi on 6 April 1930, after walking about 240 miles.
e: Started 12 March, reached Dandi and made salt on 6 April 1930.

q: The slogan 'Do or Die' is associated with which movement?
x: Gandhi gave the call 'Karo ya Maro' (Do or Die) in his speech at Gowalia Tank, Bombay, on 8 August 1942, launching the Quit India Movement.
e: Quit India: 8 August 1942, Gowalia Tank, 'Do or Die'.

q: Who gave the slogan 'Give me blood and I will give you freedom'?
x: Subhas Chandra Bose gave this call to the Indian National Army in Burma in 1944. He also coined 'Jai Hind' and 'Dilli Chalo'.
e: Bose: 'Give me blood', 'Jai Hind', 'Dilli Chalo', Azad Hind Fauj.

q: Who said 'Swaraj is my birthright and I shall have it'?
x: Bal Gangadhar Tilak gave this slogan. He was part of the Lal-Bal-Pal trio and started the Ganapati and Shivaji festivals to build public feeling.
e: Lal (Lala Lajpat Rai), Bal (Tilak), Pal (Bipin Chandra Pal) — the extremist trio.

q: The Cripps Mission came to India in which year?
x: Sir Stafford Cripps came in March 1942 offering dominion status after the war. The Congress rejected it; Gandhi called it 'a post-dated cheque'.
e: Cripps 1942 (rejected) → Quit India 1942; Cabinet Mission came in 1946.

q: Who was the last Viceroy of India?
x: Lord Mountbatten was the last Viceroy and the first Governor-General of independent India. C. Rajagopalachari was the last Governor-General, and India has never had a Viceroy since 1947.
e: Mountbatten: last Viceroy; Rajagopalachari: last Governor-General.
